description: The earliest inbound transfers of a wallet, from our own transfer tables, as TWO separate answers: `first_native_in` (the first plain send of the chain's coin to the wallet, at least `min_native` WHOLE coins; `amount` in whole coins, `amount_wei` exact in wei) and `first_token_in` (the first token transfer priced at `min_usd` USD or more; `amount` in whole tokens). Each carries the sender, its label (entity, wallet_type, label_confidence), time, tx_hash, block and `amount_usd` in plain dollars (null = no USD price). This is NOT proof of who funded the wallet: native rows hold top-level sends only (coin moved by a contract call or a bridge is absent), history starts on a different date per chain (`coverage.history_from`), and the sender may be an exchange or a relay. `found` is false when neither exists. On hyperevm, protocol system addresses appear as senders and come back with wallet_type 'system' (no entity name). Use when the user asks 'who funded this wallet' / 'where did its first coins come from', and pass the coverage caveats on.

min_native.description: Dust floor for the native coin in WHOLE coins (ETH, BNB or HYPE; 0.01 means 0.01 coin, not wei). Inbound native transfers below it are skipped. Default 0.0001; 0 = no floor (the very first inbound, probing dust included).

min_usd.description: Floor for the token side in USD. Token transfers priced below it, or with no USD price, are skipped. Default 1; 0 = no floor (unpriced tokens, mostly spam, included).

name: wallet_first_funder
title: Wallet First Funder
